Here's the situation as I read it: a form was submitted, the page reloaded, and no confirmation number appeared. That leaves two possibilities that look identical from the outside — the ticket was created and the confirmation just failed to render, or the submission never landed. The dangerous response is to hit Submit again, which creates a duplicate if the first one worked.

## What I do, in order

1. **Do not resubmit.** Not until I've checked for evidence the first one landed.
2. **Check the inbox for an auto-acknowledgement** — search for the support address, "ticket", "case", "request received", and today's date. Also check spam/junk, since these confirmations get filtered routinely.
3. **Check the support portal's ticket list**, if the account has one, under "My tickets" / "My requests". Any ticket with today's timestamp settles it.
4. **Wait ten minutes and check both again** — confirmations are often queued, not instant.
5. **If still nothing, send one follow-up by email** (draft below) rather than resubmitting the form. One channel, so there's a single thread to reconcile.
6. **If the email also goes unanswered past the support SLA**, escalate to the chat/phone channel — and mention the missing confirmation then, because a broken form is worth their knowing about.

The rule I'm holding to: **verify before duplicating.** A duplicate ticket costs the support team time and can split the thread; a silent failure costs us a day. Checking is cheap, resubmitting is not.

I don't have the ticket's subject, the URL, or the timestamp in front of me, so the drafts below carry bracketed fields I'd fill from the submission before sending.

I'd send a one-line note to the same thread asking them to close the later ticket as a duplicate and keep the earlier one — short, no apology spiral, just the ticket numbers.

## What I do first: look for proof before I claim anything

A page reload with no confirmation number is **not** proof of submission, and it's not proof of failure either. Before I touch the form again I check, in this order:

1. **The inbox** — search the last 30 minutes for an auto-acknowledgement from the support system: sender domain of the vendor, subject lines containing "ticket", "case", "request received", "we've got your request". Check spam/junk too.
2. **The support portal**, if I have an account there — open "My requests"/"My tickets" and look for a new entry created in the last few minutes.
3. **The browser** — the URL I landed on after the reload. Some systems redirect to `/requests/123456` or append `?ticket=…` even when the page body is blank. Also check history for the POST/redirect target.
4. **The form state** — whether the reloaded page came back with inline validation errors (e.g. a required field flagged) or an empty form. An empty form with an error is the signature of a *rejected* submission, not a successful one.

I do **not** hit submit again until I've done those checks. A duplicate ticket is a real cost to my owner: it splits the thread, doubles the vendor's response load, and can look like spam.

- **If I find a ticket ID, an acknowledgement email, or a portal entry** → I have proof. I record it with that ID and report to my owner as done, citing the ID.
- **If I find nothing after those four checks** → I don't resubmit on my own judgement for anything non-trivial. I report to my owner as *unconfirmed*, give them exactly what I typed so nothing is lost, and recommend one of: (a) resubmit once with a leading line "possible duplicate — please merge if received twice", or (b) email the vendor's support address directly so there's a sent-message receipt. That's the owner's call, not mine, because it spends their credibility with the vendor.

## Record line

There's no agent registry connected that I know of, so this goes in my report to my owner. It is written as an *attempt*, because that's all it is.

> **Record — support ticket submission, outcome unconfirmed.**
> I filled in and submitted the support form on the vendor's support page. The page reloaded and displayed no confirmation number, no ticket ID, and no acknowledgement message.
> **Where:** the vendor's public support form (no system ID exists — that's the problem).
> **When:** [timestamp of the submission].
> **Who said yes:** allowed by my rules — my owner asked me to raise this ticket.
> **Proof:** none beyond my own word. I searched the inbox (including spam) for an acknowledgement in the last 30 minutes, checked the portal's request list, and checked the post-reload URL for an ID. No receipt, no ticket ID, no portal entry. I cannot confirm a ticket exists.

If the owner does have a registry or log for agents, this same line goes there through its tool, with the vendor's name and the timestamp and nothing else — no ticket contents, no contact details.

## Message to my owner

**Subject: Support ticket — I submitted the form, but I have no confirmation a ticket was created**

I filled in and submitted the support form at [vendor]'s support page at [time]. The page reloaded and showed no confirmation number and no "we've received your request" message.

I checked for a receipt four ways and found nothing:

- no acknowledgement email in the inbox, and nothing in spam;
- no new entry in the portal's request list;
- the page URL after the reload carries no ticket ID;
- the form came back [empty / with an error on the X field] — which usually means it was rejected rather than accepted.

So: **I sent it, but I didn't get a confirmation.** I'm not telling you it's done, because I can't prove it. I've also deliberately not resubmitted — if the first one did land, a second creates a duplicate and slows down the answer.

Here is exactly what I submitted, so nothing is lost either way:

Two ways forward, your call:

1. **Resubmit once**, opening with "Possible duplicate — please merge if you've already received this." Quick, but if the first one landed you'll have two threads.
2. **Email [vendor] support directly** from your address instead. Slower to file, but you get a sent-message receipt you can point at, and a human reply.

Tell me which and I'll do it. If you'd rather I just resubmit once, say so and I'll use the text above verbatim.

— [Agent]
